findings.title: Login-cache invalidation uses wrapped isEnabled and keeps hidden IdPs
findings.body: update() loads the pre-update IdP with getById() and passes that object to registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(). With the ORGANIZATION feature enabled, getById() always returns the organization-aware wrapper from createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, whose isEnabled() is false unless the organization exists, OrganizationProvider.isEnabled() is true, and the organization itself is enabled. LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() (used at the checks around lines 405 and 409) treats IdentityProviderModel::isEnabled as a login-eligibility flag. So a storage-enabled, public, non-hidden org IdP fails the predicate whenever its org is disabled, missing, or the realm organization switch is off, even though delegate getForLogin still selected it using the stored enabled/linkOnly/hideOnLogin/broker-public flags and its internal id is already in the login list cache. If an update then removes login eligibility (hideOnLogin, linkOnly, or kc.org.broker.public=false) — or unlinks the IdP while also making it ineligible — both the wrapped original and the raw updated model fail the predicate, and the method returns without invalidating realmId.idp.login.{REALM_ONLY,ORG_ONLY,ALL}. The cached ids are not self-healed on the next read, because getById() still finds the row. OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only rechecks isEnabled(), not hideOnLogin, linkOnly, or broker public, so once the organization (or realm organizations switch) is turned back on, or immediately if the IdP was unlinked in the same update, that IdP is rendered on the login page. create() and remove() evaluate the predicate on the raw delegate model, so only update() is wrong. The new test only mutates realm-level IdPs and does not cover a disabled organization. Decide invalidation from the unwrapped storage model (or from config flags), not from the wrapper.

findings.title: Login-cache test cleans up a nonexistent IdP alias
findings.body: testCacheIDPForLogin creates providers aliased idp-alias-0 through idp-alias-20, but the cleanups at lines 381 and 425 call testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias") — the literal alias "alias", not the alias just created (the same mistake as the existing loop in testCacheIDPByOrg). The admin client proxy is non-null, so the test does not fail at registration, but cleanup never deletes idp-alias-*. Those providers stay in the shared test realm (half of them public and enabled, and several linked to orga). A rerun fails on duplicate aliases, and any later test that counts login or organization IdPs in the same realm sees extra brokers. Register cleanup with the actual alias (and unlink org brokers before remove).
